audit: 2026-09-15 scheduled remote agent (seventh fire of the day): one 50 question batch across all four modules, published as data/batches/sched_multi_topic_2026-09-15_g_1a.json through _g_4b.json, two files per module. Split 13 Paediatrics, 13 Obstetrics and Gynaecology, 12 Psychiatry and 12 Medicine; tier mix 28 L3 and 22 L4 with no L2 and no L5, taking the bank to 6442 with Paediatrics and Obstetrics on 1611 and Psychiatry and Medicine on 1610. Cell selection: the live matrix before this fire showed all four modules exactly level on 1598, with L3 deficits of 14.08 points in Paediatrics, 13.64 in Obstetrics, 12.83 in Medicine and 11.83 in Psychiatry, L4 deficits of 13.46, 12.96, 11.96 and 10.89 respectively, and L5 sitting at 5.006 per cent in every module, that is marginally above its 5 per cent target, so every L5 cell carried a negative deficit and generating L5 would have moved that tier away from target rather than towards it. The strict per-question argmax is degenerate for the eighth consecutive fire, and this fire established that it is degenerate in two directions rather than one: simulated across all twelve cells it pours 25 questions into Paediatrics and 25 into Obstetrics and takes the module spread from 0 to 25, breaching the Section 2 requirement that all four modules stay within about 10; constrained to a module-balanced allocation it instead returns 48 L3 and 2 L4, because L3 leads L4 by only 0.62 to 0.94 points in every module while that gap closes at roughly 0.06 points per question added. This fire therefore allocated 13/13/12/12, giving the two extra questions to the modules carrying the largest tier deficits, and split the tier mix 7 L3 with 6 L4 in Paediatrics and Obstetrics and 7 L3 with 5 L4 in Psychiatry and Medicine, which is where the tie-break clause points when it defers to the Section 2 module-balance rule. After publication L3 sits at 36.06/36.50/38.32/37.33 per cent and L4 at 31.66/32.15/34.16/33.11 per cent, with L5 at 4.97 per cent in all four modules. Structural note for the maintainer: because L5 is already at its target share, its deficit can never exceed the 11 to 14 point deficits carried by L3 and L4, so a strict argmax reading of the routine prompt will never select an L5 cell, and the L5 share will drift slowly downward as the bank grows. If continued L5 generation is wanted, the rule needs an explicit floor or per-batch quota rather than a deficit argmax. Audit: valid JSON, zero em-dashes and zero non-ASCII characters, zero banned tokens, every question difficulty 3 or 4, answer-length parity max to min at or under 1.35 on all 50, correct letters exactly 10 per letter A to E, source_refs all resolving to declared source labels, at least two sources per question with an Australian source first, reference_ranges keys all valid, vitals in fixed order or compressed to within normal limits, data_table values all flat strings, no doubled data_table, no lead-in guideline leak, no pertinent-negative parenthetical in any correct option, no correct option uniquely carrying a numeric value, no weight-based dose arithmetic in any lead-in, stems 96 to 157 words with paragraph breaks throughout, explanation.summary 3 to 5 sentences with 3 to 5 key points and a specific pearl on every question. Two craft defects were found on the first audit pass and fixed before publication: a pertinent-negative pile-up of seven closures in the monoclonal gammopathy stem, rewritten to two, and a polycythaemia item whose correct option was the only one carrying a numeral, corrected by adding numeric specificity to two distractors. scripts/dupe_gate.py --new was run against the 6392 pre-existing questions and passed with zero duplicates on the first run; intra-batch self comparison also returned zero pairs at or above 0.62, and the gate plus the full self-audit were re-run against the files fetched back from origin/main after publication, with all 50 questions confirmed identical to the audited source. Coverage: Paediatrics on an absent red reflex at the six week check, the scoliometer threshold for imaging adolescent scoliosis, treatment versus prevention dosing of cholecalciferol in nutritional rickets, chlamydial ophthalmia needing systemic rather than topical therapy, the Kocher pathway for an irritable hip, macrogol disimpaction before maintenance in overflow soiling, galactosaemia identified by urinary reducing substances with a negative glucose strip, a femoral fracture in a non-ambulant infant where blue sclerae do not close the safeguarding pathway, an unwitnessed central alpha two agonist ingestion mimicking opioid poisoning, a capillary malformation over the ophthalmic division needing brain imaging and glaucoma screening, hip surveillance in cerebral palsy acting on migration percentage rather than symptoms, an abdominal mass crossing the midline with periorbital deposits mistaken for inflicted injury, and constitutional delay confirmed by a proportionately delayed bone age;
